presentation.guidance: Narrative prose carrier; situational lead-in before optional path or code anchors; compact opening arc.

allowed.when: Single situational narrative; not ≥2 column-aligned comparable items.

forbidden: Scope, exclusion, or touch-surface enumeration tables
Architecture or flow diagrams
Before→after or success-criteria table carriers
Checkbox steps, phase markers, task ids, or verification checklist tables

required: Opens with narrative prose before path, file, or code inventories
When concrete anchors appear: they follow situational lead-in rather than opening the section
forbidden: Opening paragraphs that lead with file:line chains or path inventories

presentation.guidance: Prefer compact outcomes prose or a Before→After success-state table; at most one upstream bridging phrase.

allowed.when: One outcome narrative; not ≥2 before|after-aligned rows.

forbidden: Scope or path inventory enumeration tables
Architecture diagrams or module-responsibility graphs
Phase tables, checkbox steps, or verification command blocks
Acceptance-criteria checklists, layered L0/L1/L2 verdict tables, or AC-to-task trace tables as primary Goal carrier

required: When table carrier is used: two-column Before→After success-state view — checkable Before/After states only, not verification-step rows, acceptance-step rows, or layered verdict rows
At most one transitional bridging phrase before the outcomes block
forbidden: Multi-paragraph upstream problem narrative rehash
Observable acceptance procedures or layered behavioral test tables hosted under Goal

presentation.guidance: Prefer enumeration list or table carriers; prefer tabular or two-column layout when item count exceeds two.

allowed.when: ≤2 touch/exclusion items; not a shared-column matrix.
≥2 items sharing surface|change or in|out columns.

forbidden: Numbered invariant checklist carrier
Architecture diagram as primary carrier
Option-comparison tables with rationale columns
Phase tables, checkbox task blocks, or verification checklist rows
Host–consumer RACI matrices or collaboration-protocol essays as primary Scope carrier

required: When more than two enumeration items appear: structured or tabular carrier rather than inline prose only
Cite touch-surface file/directory paths as workspace-root markdown links (`/`-prefixed, e.g. `[frontend/app.css](/frontend/app.css)`) so they open in the editor
When the change has deferred or excluded commitments: explicit Non-Goals / out-of-scope / deferred rows or list (not only in-scope surfaces)
forbidden: Bare-backtick path citation for a touch-surface row when the path is a navigable anchor
Scope section that lists only inclusions when Non-Goals / deferred exclusions are part of the decided plan substance

presentation.guidance: Prefer diagrams for structural claims (components, control/data flow, state). Prefer short items over walls of prose for non-structural notes. Carrier priority: diagram, then table, then ordinary Markdown; fenced only for high-level literal sketches (e.g. directory tree, wireframe/ASCII layout)—never as a primary carrier.

allowed.when: Directed structure/flow; readable only as a diagram.
≥2 isomorphic structural rows under shared columns.
Brief non-structural notes; not matrix or diagram.

allowed.carrier: high-level literal sketch as a language-tagged code block
allowed.when: Literal sketch only (tree/wireframe); not primary structure.

forbidden: Diagrams without structural or flow semantics in caption or lead-in
Carriers that belong to SK, T, or VF: phase tables with Done When; checkbox or per-file edit blocks; verification checklist or trace-table carriers
Fenced blocks as the primary carrier for structure, contracts, or explanation — except high-level literal sketches
Stepwise recipe or ordered-procedure blocks as the primary Architecture carrier

required: When diagram carrier is used: structural or flow semantics stated in caption or adjacent lead-in prose
Structural claims stay at sketch depth (components, responsibility split, key interfaces/flows)
Non-structural notes are brief ordinary Markdown, not a fenced plain-text block
Non-structural notes are independently locatable and not buried as trailing content under a structural narrative
forbidden: Implementation how-to in AR (with or without paths)—belongs to T

presentation.guidance: Numbered or bulleted list carrier; each line a self-contained sentence.

allowed.when: ≥1 independent constraint; order does not matter.

forbidden: Option-comparison tables with rationale columns
Phase tables, checkbox steps, or run-command checklist rows

required: When constraint lines appear: numbered or bulleted list carrier
Each list item is a complete sentence — not pointer-only bullets
forbidden: Pointer-only bullets without constraint text in the same line

presentation.guidance: Prefer a short execution-arc lead-in, then a phase table carrier with Done When, Depends On, Parallel, and reversibility columns.

allowed.carrier: phase table with Done When, Depends On, Parallel, reversibility columns
allowed.when: ≥1 phase row with Done When column.

forbidden: Checkbox steps or task-granularity lists
Per-file change lists or Task Detail fenced blocks
Verification checklist or AC trace-table carrier

required: Execution-arc lead-in immediately before the phase table
Phase table carrier with Done When column
When dependency or reversibility facts appear in body: Depends On and reversibility as columns or row notes in the same table
Each phase-table field appears once: content/description is a short intent phrase, not a copy of Done When
forbidden: Same long Done When (or equivalent completion) prose repeated in both content and Done When cells

presentation.guidance: Prefer a Task Index table plus Change Overview per-task subsections with concrete how-to bullets and navigable path links; checkbox steps optional; never a fenced-text-only block as the sole Task Detail carrier.

allowed.carrier: Task Index with SK phase id trace column
allowed.when: ≥1 task needing SK-phase trace in an index.

allowed.carrier: Change Overview with per-task subsections and how-to bullets
Optional checkbox-step supplement under a task
allowed.when: Optional step checklist under a task; not sole task body.

forbidden: Prose-only task how-to when file paths are present in the same section
Task Detail delivered only as a fenced plain-text block
SK-style phase table with Done When columns
Verification checklist or AC trace-table carrier

required: Task Index section with SK phase id in a trace column or inline reference
Each Task Index summary states what changes (substance), not only Create/Modify / Test / type labels
Change Overview expands each task into at least one concrete how-to subsection or bullet group
Cite task file paths as workspace-root markdown links (`/`-prefixed) so they open in the editor
forbidden: Task Index rows whose summary is only a generic type label (e.g. Create/Modify, Test) with no change substance

presentation.guidance: Prefer acceptance-criteria checklist or AC table as primary carriers; use an AC-to-task-id trace table when mapping is needed.

allowed.when: Flat AC list; one criterion per row.
AC ids and task ids both present; need AC↔task columns.

forbidden: Checkbox implementation task bodies
Architecture diagram carrier
SK-style phase planning table with Done When columns
Before→After success-state table as the sole Verification carrier without acceptance or AC↔task structure

required: Checklist, AC criteria table, or AC-to-task trace-table as primary structure
When AC rows exist: AC-to-task-id mapping present (trace table or equivalent row alignment)
When AC labels and task ids both appear: row-aligned AC-to-task-id trace columns
When assumption-close rows appear: checklist rows — not SK phase tables or T checkbox bodies; explicit none if empty
forbidden: Leaving AC rows without any AC↔task traceability when task ids are defined in the plan
